This report is specifically for results from **`simu_ball_corrected_s2_conditionalX2_gexp.R`**.
Place this RMarkdown file in the folder containing your `seed*.RData` files,
then click **Knit** in RStudio. Each file should contain the numeric `res1`
vector returned by `delta()`, with all three scenarios and effects
0, 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3. No simulations are rerun by this document.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE,
                     fig.width = 10, fig.height = 3.8, dpi = 150, error = FALSE)
if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop('Install ggplot2 first: install.packages("ggplot2")')
}
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r settings}
# SETTINGS: normally these do not need changing.
# Inputs: one independent seed file per row; every file stores the same n,
# effect order, simulation settings, and 132-entry delta() layout.
# Outputs: results is a replicate-by-132 matrix; power_data contains one
# row per scenario/method/effect; figures and CSV audits use output_dir.
# Relative paths are relative to this RMarkdown file when knitted normally.
data_dir = params$data_dir
file_pattern = "^seed.*\\.(RData|rda|rds)$"
object_name = params$object_name         # object saved by job_run.R inside each .RData file
u = c(0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3)    # must match the order used when delta() was run
alpha = 0.05
allow_missing = params$allow_missing       # compatibility setting; this report counts available entries
output_dir = file.path(data_dir, "figures_ball_corrected")

# Each list contains positions WITHIN the 44-entry scenario block.
common_indices = list(
  "Proposed-plm" = 17:20,
  "Proposed-t-test" = c(1, 3, 5, 7),
  "Proposed-lm" = c(9, 11, 13, 15),
  "Naive-t-test" = c(2, 4, 6, 8),
  "Naive-lm" = c(10, 12, 14, 16)
)
method_indices = list(
  c(common_indices, list("Ma2022mr"=25:28, "Ma2015lm"=41:44, "Ye2018plm"=33:36)),
  c(common_indices, list("Ma2022mr"=41:44, "Ma2015lm"=25:28, "Ye2018plm"=33:36)),
  c(common_indices, list("Ma2022mr"=25:28, "Ma2015lm"=41:44, "Ye2018plm"=33:36))
)
method_functions = list(
  c("Proposed-plm"="testbs3.dis", "Proposed-t-test"="testbs1.dis (adjusted)",
    "Proposed-lm"="testbs2.dis (adjusted)", "Naive-t-test"="testbs1.dis (naive)",
    "Naive-lm"="testbs2.dis (naive)", "Ma2022mr"="ftest2.dis",
    "Ma2015lm"="fftest2.dis", "Ye2018plm"="testye2.dis"),
  c("Proposed-plm"="testbs3.ind", "Proposed-t-test"="testbs1.ind (adjusted)",
    "Proposed-lm"="testbs2.ind (adjusted)", "Naive-t-test"="testbs1.ind (naive)",
    "Naive-lm"="testbs2.ind (naive)", "Ma2022mr"="fftest2.mf.ind",
    "Ma2015lm"="fftest2.ind", "Ye2018plm"="testye2.ind"),
  c("Proposed-plm"="testbs3.ts", "Proposed-t-test"="testbs1.ts (adjusted)",
    "Proposed-lm"="testbs2.ts (adjusted)", "Naive-t-test"="testbs1.ts (naive)",
    "Naive-lm"="testbs2.ts (naive)", "Ma2022mr"="ftest2.c3",
    "Ma2015lm"="fftest2.ts", "Ye2018plm"="testye2.ts")
)

```

```{r read-data}
files = list.files(data_dir, pattern = file_pattern,
                   full.names = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
if (length(files) == 0L) {
  stop("No seed*.RData / seed*.rda / seed*.rds files found in: ",
       normalizePath(data_dir),
       ". Put this Rmd beside the result files, or edit data_dir/file_pattern.")
}
# Sort seed numbers for a readable input manifest; averaging is order invariant.
seed_text = sub("^seed([0-9]+).*", "\\1", basename(files), ignore.case = TRUE)
seed_number = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(seed_text))
file_order = order(seed_number, basename(files), na.last = TRUE)
files = files[file_order]
# The filename stems provide a second duplicate check across RData/RDS formats.
stems = tolower(tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(files)))
canonical = sub("^seed0*([0-9]+)$", "seed\\1", stems)
if (anyDuplicated(canonical)) {
  stop("Duplicate seed filenames detected (possibly both RData and RDS copies).",
       " Keep only one result file per simulation replicate.")
}
if (length(u) != 4L || any(!is.finite(u)) || anyDuplicated(u)) {
  stop("This report expects four distinct finite effects in the saved delta() order.")
}
# delta() returns 44 entries per scenario: 8+8+4+4+4+4+4+4+4.
expected_length = 132L
#' Read and validate one saved simulation replicate
#'
#' Load the result vector from an RDS file or from object_name inside an RData/rda file,
#' using a private environment for the latter.
#'
#' @param path Character scalar path to one seed result file.
#' @return Length-expected_length numeric vector with entries 0, 1, or NA, ready to
#'   become one row of results. Missing objects, invalid lengths, batch matrices, or
#'   nonbinary finite values cause an error.
#' @details Uses object_name and expected_length from the report settings. A one-column
#'   matrix is accepted and flattened; no simulation is rerun.
read_one = function(path) {
  if (tolower(tools::file_ext(path)) == "rds") {
    value = readRDS(path)
  } else {
    env = new.env(parent = emptyenv())
    objects = load(path, envir = env)
    if (!(object_name %in% objects)) {
      stop(basename(path), " does not contain '", object_name,
           "'. Objects found: ", paste(objects, collapse = ", "))
    }
    value = env[[object_name]]
  }
  if (!is.numeric(value) || length(value) != expected_length ||
      (!is.null(dim(value)) && sum(dim(value) > 1L) > 1L)) {
    stop(basename(path), ": expected one numeric length-132 delta() vector.",
         " Do not mix summaries, batch matrices, or other simulation outputs.")
  }
  value = as.numeric(value)
  if (any(!is.na(value) & !(value %in% c(0, 1)))) {
    stop(basename(path), ": entries must be rejection indicators 0/1 (or NA).")
  }
  value
}
# Stack validated vectors without changing their within-scenario ordering.
results = do.call(rbind, lapply(files, read_one))
rownames(results) = basename(files)
# Identify plotted columns and audit missing entries across ALL saved columns.
# Column callback: input scenario is an integer from 1 to 3; output is
# the global delta() column numbers used by that scenario in these plots.
plotted_columns = sort(unique(unlist(lapply(1:3, function(scenario)
  (scenario - 1L) * 44L + unlist(method_indices[[scenario]], use.names = FALSE)))))
missing_by_column = data.frame(
  Delta_index = seq_len(ncol(results)),
  Scenario = (seq_len(ncol(results)) - 1L) %/% 44L + 1L,
  Within_scenario_index = (seq_len(ncol(results)) - 1L) %% 44L + 1L,
  Used_in_plots = seq_len(ncol(results)) %in% plotted_columns,
  Missing = colSums(is.na(results)),
  Available = colSums(!is.na(results)))
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(missing_by_column, file.path(output_dir, "missing_results_by_column.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
missing_total = sum(is.na(results))
missing_plotted = sum(is.na(results[, plotted_columns, drop = FALSE]))

manifest = data.frame(file = basename(files),
                      missing_entries = rowSums(is.na(results)))
write.csv(manifest, file.path(output_dir, "input_manifest.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

The complete saved output contains **`r missing_total` missing entries**, of which
**`r missing_plotted` belong to methods used in these plots**. Missing values in
unplotted methods do not exclude any datasets from the plotted methods. All 132
columns are audited in `figures_ball_corrected/missing_results_by_column.csv`.

## Reading the saved output

`r nrow(results)` result files were loaded. Each file is treated as one independent
simulation replicate. Do not combine files produced with different sample sizes,
data-generating mechanisms, or tuning settings in the same report. These settings are
not encoded in an unnamed `res1` vector and cannot be checked automatically.

The mapping follows `delta()` in `simu_ball_corrected_s2_conditionalX2_gexp.R`. **Scenario 2 has a
different comparator order:** `Ma2022mr` uses positions 41--44 and `Ma2015lm`
uses 25--28 within its scenario block. In Scenarios 1 and 3 these positions
are reversed. `Ye2018plm` uses 33--36 in all scenarios. The unadjusted comparison
variants in positions 21--24, 29--32, and 37--40 are not plotted.

An unnamed length-132 vector cannot identify its generating code or settings.
Use only files from the corrected all-covariate simulation, with the same n
and tuning choices. No externally supplied values replace any saved results.

```{r method-mapping}
# Mapping callback: input scenario is an integer from 1 to 3; output is
# one data frame of method names, local/global indices, and function names.
mapping_table = do.call(rbind, lapply(1:3, function(scenario) {
  indices = method_indices[[scenario]]
  data.frame(
    Scenario = paste("Scenario", scenario),
    Method = names(indices),
    Within_scenario_indices = vapply(indices, paste, collapse = ", ", FUN.VALUE = character(1)),
    # Index-format callback: input x is the four local effect indices;
    # output is one character string listing their global delta() positions.
    Delta_indices = vapply(indices, function(x) paste((scenario-1L)*44L+x, collapse=", "), character(1)),
    Function = unname(method_functions[[scenario]][names(indices)]),
    row.names = NULL
  )
}))
write.csv(mapping_table, file.path(output_dir, "method_mapping.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(mapping_table, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r summarize-data}
# For each saved column, divide rejection count by its available replicates.
# MCSE is sqrt(p_hat * (1-p_hat) / R_valid), the SE of the outer simulation mean.
# Exact 95% binomial limits describe Monte Carlo uncertainty in that rate.
summary_rows = list()
k = 0L
for (scenario in 1:3) {
  for (method in names(method_indices[[scenario]])) {
    for (j in seq_along(u)) {
      column = (scenario - 1L) * 44L + method_indices[[scenario]][[method]][j]
      values = results[, column]
      n_valid = sum(!is.na(values))
      if (n_valid == 0L) {
        stop("No valid results for Scenario ", scenario, ", ", method,
             ", effect = ", u[j])
      }
      rejected = sum(values, na.rm = TRUE)
      estimate = rejected / n_valid
      # Exact binomial intervals remain informative at observed rates 0 and 1.
      interval = binom.test(rejected, n_valid, conf.level = 0.95)$conf.int
      k = k + 1L
      summary_rows[[k]] = data.frame(
        Scenario = paste("Scenario", scenario),
        Method = method, Effect = u[j], Power = estimate,
        Rejections = rejected, Replicates = n_valid,
        Missing = length(values) - n_valid,
        MCSE = sqrt(estimate * (1 - estimate) / n_valid),
        MC_lower = interval[1], MC_upper = interval[2],
        Delta_index = column
      )
    }
  }
}
# Assemble the summaries and retain the source Delta_index for traceability.
power_data = do.call(rbind, summary_rows)
power_data$Scenario = factor(power_data$Scenario,
                             levels = paste("Scenario", 1:3))
write.csv(power_data, file.path(output_dir, "power_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

At zero effect the rejection rate estimates **type I error**. At nonzero effects
it estimates **power**. The blue horizontal line marks the nominal 5% level.
Monte Carlo intervals and the number of valid replicates are saved in
`figures_ball_corrected/power_summary.csv`; intervals are omitted from the figures to match the
provided examples. An estimated MCSE of zero at an observed rate of 0 or 1 does
not mean there is no uncertainty; use the exact interval columns in that case.

```{r plot-theme}
# Reuse the same axes, facet strips, and legend appearance in both figures.
common_theme = theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#D9D9D9", colour = "#888888"),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12, colour = "black"),
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "#888888", fill = NA),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#EAEAEA", linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(colour = "#F3F3F3", linewidth = 0.25),
    panel.spacing.x = grid::unit(0.12, "in"),
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "#555555"),
    axis.title = element_text(colour = "black"),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.key.width = grid::unit(0.65, "cm"),
    plot.margin = margin(6, 6, 6, 6)
  )

#' Build the common faceted power-plot layout
#'
#' Create the shared ggplot before the caller adds method-specific colours, shapes, and
#' line types.
#'
#' @param data Summary data frame with Effect (numeric treatment effect), Power
#'   (rejection rate), Method (method label), and Scenario (facet label).
#' @return A ggplot object with method lines and points, one facet per scenario, and a
#'   horizontal reference at alpha. The function does not save the plot.
#' @details Uses alpha, u, and common_theme from the surrounding report. At Effect = 0,
#'   Power is the empirical type I error. MCSE and binomial intervals remain in the
#'   summary table; this plot uses point estimates.
base_plot = function(data) {
  ggplot(data, aes(x = Effect, y = Power, colour = Method,
                   linetype = Method, shape = Method, group = Method)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = alpha, colour = "blue", linewidth = 0.45) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.65) +
    geom_point(size = 1.9, stroke = 0.65) +
    facet_wrap(~ Scenario, nrow = 1) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = u, labels = sprintf("%.1f", u),
                       expand = expansion(mult = 0.035)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                       labels = sprintf("%.2f", seq(0, 1, 0.25)),
                       expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.025, 1.025)) +
    labs(x = expression(u[2] - u[1]), y = "Power",
         colour = "Method", linetype = "Method", shape = "Method") +
    common_theme
}
```

## Proposed methods and naive tests

```{r figure-one}
methods_1 = c("Proposed-plm", "Proposed-t-test", "Proposed-lm",
              "Naive-t-test", "Naive-lm")
data_1 = power_data[power_data$Method %in% methods_1, ]
data_1$Method = factor(data_1$Method, levels = methods_1)

plot_1 = base_plot(data_1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
    "Proposed-plm" = "#F8766D", "Proposed-t-test" = "#00BFC4",
    "Proposed-lm" = "#E5A44A", "Naive-t-test" = "#C77CFF",
    "Naive-lm" = "#FFB3BA"), breaks = methods_1) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "solid", "solid", "dashed", "dashed"),
                        breaks = methods_1) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = rep(16, 5), breaks = methods_1)
plot_1
```

## Proposed PLM and comparison methods

```{r figure-two}
methods_2 = c("Proposed-plm", "Ma2022mr", "Ma2015lm", "Ye2018plm")
data_2 = power_data[power_data$Method %in% methods_2, ]
data_2$Method = factor(data_2$Method, levels = methods_2)

plot_2 = base_plot(data_2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
    "Proposed-plm" = "#F8766D", "Ma2022mr" = "#FDAE6B",
    "Ma2015lm" = "#4DB6AC", "Ye2018plm" = "#607D8B"), breaks = methods_2) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "dashed", "dashed", "dashed"),
                        breaks = methods_2) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = rep(16, 4), breaks = methods_2)
plot_2
```

```{r save-figures, include=FALSE}
# Edit width/height here if your manuscript requires different dimensions.
for (ext in c("png", "pdf")) {
  ggsave(file.path(output_dir, paste0("proposed_vs_naive.", ext)),
         plot = plot_1, width = 10, height = 3.8, units = "in",
         dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  ggsave(file.path(output_dir, paste0("proposed_vs_comparators.", ext)),
         plot = plot_2, width = 10, height = 3.8, units = "in",
         dpi = 300, bg = "white")
}
```

## Type I error at zero effect

```{r type-i-table}
null_results = power_data[power_data$Effect == 0,
  c("Scenario", "Method", "Power", "Rejections", "Replicates", "Missing",
    "MC_lower", "MC_upper")]
names(null_results)[names(null_results) == "Power"] = "Type_I_error"
knitr::kable(null_results, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
```

The two PNGs, two PDFs, summary CSV, method-mapping CSV, and input manifest are saved in the
`figures_ball_corrected` subfolder. Curve values are calculated from your result files, not
copied from the reference images. The x-axis shows the absolute treatment-effect difference, consistent with the
nonnegative effect values and two-sided tests.
